..when they're talking about me, it's like [Swiss gibberish] Facebook, and then when it's about Critter, it's like [Swiss gibberish] bodyguard. And another thing -- when people meet Critter, whose name is Christopher -- when Pamela Adlon was on the show and she met Critter, she's...

His older brother. So fast, it sounds like 'Critter-fer.' And then everyone, I guess, assumed he was calling me Critter. So it's been Critter since I was, like, a baby. Oh, so do your parents call you Critter?

No, my mom and my dad call me Christopher, but everyone else pretty much calls me Critter. And what happens when people make fun of your stuttering brother? They usually get beaten. He's being shy right now, but basically Critter's older brother stutters -- Dan stutters, and Critter has a speech impediment, problems saying R's, S's, W's.

Do you? Uh huh. I never noticed. A lot of people think I'm from, like, the South. Yeah, he's got a -- I got my Southern twang. Yeah, he's got a twang to his talk. But it's actually a speech impediment. Yeah. So, Critter...
..you know, his older brother stutters and can't pronounce his name, so people love -- it's, I don't know. I've never met your brother, and I don't know how bad his stutter is. Oh, it's fine now.

I mean, he does it on occasion, but... But his older brother stutters, and so when people would make fun of him, Critter would -- Critter Skillet -- Critter, Creature, would beat the living shit out of them, which is pretty cool.

Aww. Yeah. And also, when I was young, my parents couldn't even understand me, so my brother was the only one that could understand me. So they'd be like, what is he saying? And he'd be like, he wants two ice creams.
He wants two slices of pizza. So you were his translator? No -- oh, he was your translator. For me. But he used it to his advantage. He'd be like, oh, he wants two candy bars.
How much older is he than you? He's two years older than me, and I have a younger sister that's, like, two years younger. And no speech impediment on her end?

No, she's perfect, she's the little princess. My little brother had to go to speech class. We went on vacation, and he said, 'Mommy, are we gonna sweep you tonight?' And he had to go to speech class for that. What am I thinking about right now? Mine was great, because...

..the way they try and deal with it is, I would have to suck on suckers to get my tongue to go up to the top of my mouth. So I had to eat candy all day long. Oh, hence your love of snacks! That's pretty cool, so you got to eat snacks all the time. Yeah. What does it mean when you have a speech impediment?

Like, is it a physical thing? I mean, I guess it means I don't talk -- 'how, how, how bad was this.' Like, I just did that right now. Yeah, that's like a stutter, a minor stutter. Yeah. No, I know a few people with stutters, like, in their adult lives. He stutters. Like, how bad? I want to know how bad.
More when he's nervous? No, it's actually not when he's nervous. He does it, you know, like when we're out drinking or something, he'll just get, like -- stuck on one word.
Yeah, you know, he'll be like... But what he'll usually do is just go use a different word that comes right out. Oh, he catches himself? He like knows he can't say that word.

He catches himself, yeah. Like, he'll start to do it, and then he'll just switch it around. Does he have any other disabilities or problems? No. I wonder what that means, where that comes from. Will you fucking stop doing that? It's driving me crazy. Jesus. I'm just seeing this thing. Bobby -- if Bobby was here, I could -- Bobby, where the fuck are you, man? Where is Bobby?

He looked really busy when he was -- Push that fucking chair out of the way, it's driving me crazy. You can't sit still for, like, two seconds. Wait, no, we can't see you, just move the chair. Yeah, just, like, right there. So, um -- I go, yeah, okay, cool. So she's like, when you...

..fly in, we'll have a dinner for you, and you'll meet, like, six of the students that were crucial in helping make this happen. Alright, whatever, that's cool. And I don't remember any of their names, but this guy comes, and he's like, [imitating stutter] 'nnn-nnn-nnn-night'... and I was like...

..it drove me crazy. This guy would get stuck on a word, because you want to say it for him -- Yeah -- and I'm like, oh, it's like you're rooting for a team or something, you're like, fuck, he's almost there, he's like -- and I was like, oh my god...

..please get to the word. And then he gets there, and it's like [exhales] -- then you let go. Yeah, like you're holding your breath, and then you're like [gasps]. And I was like, this is crazy, because I've never met anyone that had, like, that level of a cartoon stutter. And then his girlfriend showed up, and she had it...
..too. And they sat -- I was at the end, you're there, like, you're the guest, sit at the end of the table. I've never met a girl with a stutter. He was white, she was Asian.
She sat here, he sat here, and they were both talking to me. And it was -- it's fucking crazy. It's like...

It's like -- if you lived in London for five years, there's a kind of person that would just never pick it up, and then there's a type of person that would, like, talk with a British accent after that.

At the end of that dinner -- you were stuttering. I was stuttering! I was, like, second-guessing words and shit. I was like, oh my god, it was like stereo stutter. And I was like, this is crazy. Do they stutter when they're alone with each other, though? I wonder. I don't know, man, but I was like, this is...

..fucking nuts, I've never seen anything like that. Yeah, that's like with my brother -- he won't do it for, like, ever, and then he'll just do it, and then it's like, you don't know if I should say the word, because I usually know what he's trying to say. Can you get your feet off...

I think they want to get it out, because I think it's kind of like old people. Old people don't want you to help them down the stairs, help them up. So I think it's kind of the same thing.

They want to get it out. So we should just patiently wait. Yeah, I mean, it's actually pretty thrilling -- it's like being on a ride. Because the stutter -- Right, I do know what you mean, where you hold your breath and wait for them to say it, you're like, please -- and when they let it out, you're like, yeah! I totally know what you mean.
